notes: Two reports, as NSS combines them for Arizona's peak-flow group (NSS region 5). (1) Paretti, Kennedy, Turney and Veilleux, SIR 2014-5211 (no revisions listed): flood regions 1-4 at 8 AEPs (50-0.2 percent), equations from Table 9 (pp. 28-29), MSE/SEP/pseudo-R2/SEM/AVP from Table 10 (pp. 30-31), ranges and number of sites from Table 11 (p. 33), and MEV, t and covariance U from Table 12 in SIR2014-5211_tables.xlsx. REGION 5 (Southeastern Basin and Range) IS NOT STORED: its equations have the form Q = 10^(a - b DRNAREA^-c) (Table 9), i.e. a raw power of drainage area inside the log-linear sum, which the schema's transforms (identity or log10 of scale*x + offset) cannot express; Table 10's statistics and Table 12's 2x2 matrices exist for it. NSS also rounds region 5's 4-percent b, printed 2.988, to 2.99. Storage: intercept = log10 of the printed coefficient; drainage area uses NSS's code CONTDA (the report's 'DRNAREA', GIS contributing drainage area; NSS's Arizona regions use CONTDA), log10; PRECIP (mean annual precipitation, in.) log10; the term 10^(c ELEV/1,000) is ELEV with transform identity, scale 0.001 and coefficient c, which is also Table 12's basis ('ELEV/1000'). Region 3 drops ELEV at 4 percent and rarer AEPs (Table 9; Table 11 footnote a lists only 4, 1, 0.5 and 0.2, omitting 2, but Table 9 and Table 12 have no ELEV at 2 percent either), and region 4's 50-percent equation uses drainage area alone. Table 11 prints region 2's drainage-area maximum as '1,6017'; NSS uses 16,017, and 16,017 is stored. Error statistics: model_error_variance is Table 12's MEV (full precision; it equals Table 10's SEM converted to log10 units squared within 0.002); avp is Table 10's AVP (log10 units squared, 3 decimals); sep_log is Table 10's SEP (percent) converted as sqrt(ln(1 + (SEP/100)^2)) / ln(10) (the inverse of the report's eq. 7); covariance is Table 12's U = (X^T Lambda^-1 X)^-1 in the order intercept, DRNAREA, PRECIP, ELEV/1000 as labelled, copied at full precision; n_sites is Table 11's number of sites (41, 85, 68, 77); Table 12's t values correspond to n - p degrees of freedom. Checks: the p. 34 worked example (region 4 Q1 at USGS 09508500, DRNAREA 5,499, PRECIP 19.6, ELEV 5,573) gives 149,714 ft3/s as printed, SEp,i 0.1104 (printed 0.1105; x'Ux 0.001322 against the printed 0.0013066, which the report computed from unrounded StreamStats characteristics), and a 90-percent interval of 98,000-229,000 ft3/s as printed (t = 1.666 from Table 12). Table 14's regression estimates at the regression gages (Table 1 characteristics) agree with the equations at the median within 0.7 percent in every region and AEP, 2,517 of 2,616 values within 1 percent; the rest are a few large or redundant gages whose Table 1 characteristics evidently differ from the regression inputs. MEV + x'Ux reproduces Table 13's regression variance of prediction within 3-decimal rounding at 1,713 of 2,128 site-AEPs, and MEV + mean x'Ux reproduces Table 10's AVP within 0.0021. NSS selects region 1 (High Elevation) when ELEV is 7,500 ft or more and regions 2 and 5 below; ELEV is not a regression variable there. (2) Waltemeyer, SIR 2006-5306 (Navajo Nation): regions 8, 11 and High Elevation, which NSS lists for Arizona (GC843-GC845), stored exactly as in CO.json, UT.json and NM.json. Values were double-entered (hand transcription from rendered pages vs. a programmatic parse of the PDF text) with zero disagreements, and every stored region and AEP equals live NSS at its 3 significant figures.
